Now, there's some overlapping but I couldn't play a modern line against a traditional rhythm section or play a traditional line against a modern rhythm section. And if it's a swing group, I'll play more or less in that style. And, of course, my ideal is to combine the best of all of them if I can, ultimately. ... ... ... ... ... ...

segments.title: Interview opening and topic set-up
segments.summary: Allen records date, place and name, and steers the talk to Kmen's scholarly work on New Orleans.

segments.title: Why jazz began in New Orleans: dancing, race and street parades
segments.summary: Kmen argues New Orleans' dance mania, Black dance musicians and parade bands produced jazz.

segments.title: Pre-Civil War New Orleans as America's musical center
segments.summary: New Orleans led the nation musically; the French Opera toured northern cities and introduced instruments.

segments.title: Opera, the Philharmonic Society and boatmen in the balconies
segments.summary: Opera was the main classical endeavor; the only permanent resident opera company, with boatmen filling the galleries.

segments.title: Rival theaters and their French and American audiences
segments.summary: The Camp Street and St. Charles theaters competed with the French Orleans Theater for audiences.

segments.title: Slaves and free Negroes at balls and theaters
segments.summary: Slaves worked for wages, lived on their own and mixed with free Negroes at dances and the opera.

segments.title: Bands at boxing, fireworks, churches and races
segments.summary: They discuss whether bands played at boxing matches and racing; Kmen notes bands at fireworks, dances and church services.

segments.title: Music and dancing at the lake hotels and Bay St. Louis
segments.summary: Lake hotels had dance music, and special cruise boats ran to Bay St. Louis.

segments.title: Newspaper research progress, slave balls and Black musicians for white dances
segments.summary: Kmen describes his newspaper research, slave balls, and Black musicians playing white dances but not vice versa.

segments.title: White musicians and the French opera orchestra turnover
segments.summary: Few white men aspired to be performers, but opera musicians stayed on as teachers and dance promoters.

segments.title: Social class and respect for early musicians
segments.summary: Discussion of the social class of early musicians, subscription balls versus brawls, and respect for musicians.

segments.title: Why dance music became a Black specialty
segments.summary: Kmen argues white men had better opportunities, so dance music became a Black trade.

segments.title: Military funerals and the roots of funeral bands
segments.summary: Militia and fraternal funerals, complaints about unseemly music, and Black burial societies.

segments.title: Kmen's birth and Saratoga's summer bands
segments.summary: Born 1915 in Saratoga Springs, where big bands played the gambling houses each summer.

segments.title: Hotel bands, territory bands and how bands rose
segments.summary: Whiteman and Lopez at Saratoga, territory bands, the Les Brown origin and shifting personnel.

segments.title: Starting piano and C-melody saxophone
segments.summary: Kmen took piano lessons, took up a C-melody saxophone around 1927 and read sheet music.

segments.title: Learning by sitting in with Black and white bands upstate
segments.summary: Kmen learned by sitting in; no color bars upstate and Black musicians shared tricks freely.

segments.title: Paul Tremaine's band and early swing impressions
segments.summary: Kmen recalls the Paul Tremaine band as a relaxed forerunner of swing, compared with Casa Loma.

segments.title: Saxophone idols such as Coleman Hawkins
segments.summary: Hawkins was the early idol of saxophonists; the block degrades into repeated garbage text.

segments.title: Pre-swing big bands and saxophonists admired
segments.summary: Pre-swing bands groping toward swing; Pat Davis and Hutchinrider are recalled.

segments.chapter: New York 1930s and New Orleans expatriates
segments.title: New Orleans style seen as corny; meeting Shields and Parenti
segments.summary: Kmen moved to New York in 1933-34, met Larry Shields and Tony Parenti at Sharkey's apartment.

segments.chapter: New York 1930s and New Orleans expatriates
segments.title: First hearing Benny Goodman and Adrian Rollini
segments.summary: Goodman's first records and a Skidmore College dance; Adrian Rollini's pocket reed instrument.

segments.chapter: New York 1930s and New Orleans expatriates
segments.title: Larry Shields's clarinet influence
segments.summary: Shields's playing was universally respected and influenced imitators of the Dixieland Band.

segments.chapter: New York 1930s and New Orleans expatriates
segments.title: Unsung musicians and Sharkey's band at the Nick's
segments.summary: Kmen recalls Black bands in Saratoga, then Sharkey's New Orleans band at Nick's.

segments.chapter: New York 1930s and New Orleans expatriates
segments.title: Bobby Hackett and Brunis
segments.summary: Kmen talks about playing with Hackett, who could never play loud, and the move to the new Nick's.

segments.chapter: New York 1930s and New Orleans expatriates
segments.title: Sitting in around New York and Adrian's Tap Room
segments.summary: Kmen sat in at Nick's and Adrian's Tap Room; recalls Artie Drillinger and Lyman Bunk.

segments.chapter: New York 1930s and New Orleans expatriates
segments.title: Forgotten names, Fazola and Eddie Miller's low clarinet
segments.summary: Kmen forgets names, then discusses Fazola with Crosby and Eddie Miller's low-register clarinet chorus.

segments.chapter: New York 1930s and New Orleans expatriates
segments.title: Clarinet registers, Crosby band and record identification
segments.summary: Further talk of low-register clarinet, Dixieland trio choruses and a hazy record identification.

segments.title: Depression struggles, club dates and Joe Marcella
segments.summary: Hard times in New York, club dates, Prima's band and the Marcella brothers; Dorr's unpaid wages.

segments.title: New Orleans musicians homesick in New York
segments.summary: Most New Orleans musicians pined for home; Kmen recalls spot jobs with Bill Bourgeois.

segments.title: Pickup bands and booking practices
segments.summary: Leaders booked many jobs and sent substitutes; musicians read stocks.

segments.title: What makes a band's or player's style
segments.summary: Section sounds, stock arrangements and the tone, environment and ideals that shape style.

segments.title: Kmen's own style across groups
segments.summary: Kmen adapts his playing to modern, swing or traditional groups.
